statement.p: If C is the line segment from (6,5) to, (0,0), find the value of the line integral:

p.m: \int_C (2 y^2\,\vec i + 3 x\,\vec j)\cdot d\vec r =

static.solution:
(0,0) to (6,5) and then take the negative. The line segment is parameterized by x = 6 t\quad y = 5 t, \qquad \mbox{for } 0\le t\le 1.
Then \vec r'(t)=6\vec i+ 5\vec j, so \int_C (2 y^2\,\vec i + 3 x\,\vec j)\cdot d\vec r =-\int_0^1\left(50 t^2\,\vec i + 18 t\,\vec j \right)\cdot (6\vec i+5\vec j)\, dt =-\int_0^1(300 t^2 + 90 t)\, dt=-\left(100 t^3 + 45 t^2\right)\bigg|_0^1 = -145.
